fields.statement: Machine trust serves milestone-24, the dedicated-VM milestone
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.statement: A machine's trust lives in a machine config file, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rhiza/machine.toml (default ~/.config/rhiza/machine.toml), as trust = "dedicated" or "daily"; it is outside every repo, so no clone carries it
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.statement: Trust is set only by hand-editing the machine config: rhiza has no command or API operation that writes it, so no agent raises trust through rhiza
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.statement: No machine config means trust = daily; a malformed file or an unknown trust value is an error naming the file, and bypass stays refused
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.statement: Trust changes no default permission mode: on a dedicated machine it only stops refusing a mode that bypasses the agent's checks, and the mode stays explicit
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.statement: Trust shows in a read-only rhiza machine show and in a machine part of rhiza health
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.statement: Trust is read fresh from the machine config at every check (session start, session run, run start and resume, daemon start), and no session record or journal carries it
fields.wording: (assumed for the owner by the orchestrator acting as their proxy, the agent's option picked by the orchestrator)

fields.acceptance: Go tests over the machine config reader: no file gives daily; trust = "dedicated" and trust = "daily" read as such, from XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set and ~/.config otherwise; a file that is not TOML, or trust = "root", is an error naming the file's path
fields.statement: Rhiza reads a per-machine config at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rhiza/machine.toml (default ~/.config/rhiza/machine.toml) whose trust is "dedicated" or "daily", daily when the file is absent, and a malformed file or unknown trust is an error naming the file

fields.acceptance: A testscript with trust = "dedicated" in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rhiza/machine.toml starts a session and a run with --permission-mode bypassPermissions on a fake adapter and the launch logs bypassPermissions; with no file, and again after the file is changed to trust = "daily" between session start and session run, both refuse with the error naming the file and nothing is launched; the existing autonomous-permissions refusal still passes with no machine config
fields.statement: On a machine whose config has trust = "dedicated", session start, session run, run start and resume, and the daemon accept a permission mode that bypasses the agent's checks; on any other machine they refuse it, the error naming the machine config file and the line trust = "dedicated", and trust is read fresh at each check

fields.acceptance: A testscript runs rhiza machine show with no file (daily, no machine config), with trust = "dedicated" (dedicated and the path) and with a bad file (exit non-zero naming the file), and --json matches rhiza api call; describe --json lists no operation that writes the machine config
fields.statement: rhiza machine show (and its API op) prints the machine's trust and the config file it came from, or daily with no machine config, and writes nothing; rhiza has no operation that writes trust

fields.acceptance: A testscript runs rhiza health --json with no machine config, with trust = "dedicated" and with a bad file, and finds a machine part that is ok with daily, ok with dedicated, and warn naming the file
fields.statement: rhiza health and the Health app show a machine part: ok with the trust and its file, or daily with no machine config, and warn naming the file when the machine config cannot be read
